events.title: Aetius checks Attila at the Catalaunian Plains
events.description: A coalition of Romans and Visigoths under Aetius fought Attila's Huns to a halt in Gaul, on a date traditionally given as 20 June. Attila withdrew, and invaded Italy the following year.
events.html: A coalition of Romans and Visigoths under Aetius fought Attila's Huns to a halt in Gaul, on a date traditionally given as 20 June. Attila withdrew, and invaded Italy the following year.

events.title: British captives are confined in the 'Black Hole of Calcutta'
events.description: After the Nawab of Bengal took Calcutta, British prisoners were held overnight in a tiny guardroom, where many died. The numbers are disputed, but the story fuelled British retaliation.
events.html: After the Nawab of Bengal took Calcutta, British prisoners were held overnight in a tiny guardroom, where many died. The numbers are disputed, but the story fuelled British retaliation.

events.title: Third Estate swears the Tennis Court Oath
events.description: Locked out of their hall, deputies of the National Assembly met in a royal tennis court at Versailles and vowed not to separate until France had a constitution.
events.html: Locked out of their hall, deputies of the National Assembly met in a royal tennis court at Versailles and vowed not to separate until France had a constitution.

events.title: Victoria becomes queen at the age of 18
events.description: Victoria was woken at Kensington Palace with news that William IV had died. Her 63-year reign saw industrial growth and the expansion of the British Empire.
events.html: Victoria was woken at Kensington Palace with news that William IV had died. Her 63-year reign saw industrial growth and the expansion of the British Empire.

events.title: US and Soviet Union agree to set up a hotline
events.description: Signed in Geneva after the Cuban Missile Crisis, the agreement created a direct teletype link between Washington and Moscow. Popularly called the 'red telephone', it was never a telephone.
events.html: Signed in Geneva after the Cuban Missile Crisis, the agreement created a direct teletype link between Washington and Moscow. Popularly called the 'red telephone', it was never a telephone.

events.title: Bundestag votes to move Germany's government to Berlin
events.description: By 338 votes to 320, the parliament of reunified Germany chose Berlin over Bonn as the seat of government. The move was completed in 1999.
events.html: By 338 votes to 320, the parliament of reunified Germany chose Berlin over Bonn as the seat of government. The move was completed in 1999.

intl.name: World Refugee Day
intl.description: Designated by the UN General Assembly in 2001 to coincide with the 50th anniversary of the 1951 Refugee Convention, World Refugee Day honours the courage and resilience of the more than 100 million forcibly displaced people worldwide.
